The contributor certification template requires contributor_name identifying the person or organization submitting the data.
The template requires contribution_description giving a short description of the submitted data or artifact.
The template requires source_name for public data records, matching docs/IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md required provenance fields.
The template requires source_location (URL, path, document identifier) or TBD.
The template requires source_license stating the redistribution basis, or TBD when unresolved.
The template requires redistribution_status as one of public_permissive, private_only, unknown, or protected_suspected.

The contributor_certification field states the contribution is original, permissively redistributable, or submitted with documented rights, and that no protected standards/proprietary content is copied unless rights are documented.
The protected_content_screen field records whether protected standards text/tables/figures/examples, copied formulas, protected dimensional tables, or proprietary catalog data appear suspected.
The private_data_screen field records whether user-private project, owner, rule-pack, material, or component data is present.
The review_status field is one of pending, accepted, rejected, or quarantined.
The reviewer field records maintainer/reviewer identity at disposition; final role assignment remains TBD.
The disposition_notes field records at disposition a short rationale and links to evidence, issue, or quarantine record.
Review routing state Intake pending means the contribution has not yet passed completeness/provenance screening.
Review routing state Provenance review means source, license, redistribution status, and contributor attestation are being checked.
Review routing state Protected-content review means the contribution is blocked pending protected-content/private-data review.
Review routing state Quarantined means suspected protected or private content has been isolated outside public examples.
Review routing state Accepted for public repo means the reviewer recorded a public redistribution basis and found no protected/private-data blocker.
Review routing state Rejected means the contribution cannot be accepted under current evidence.

The workflow separates open mechanics and permissibly redistributable public data from protected standards-body content, proprietary vendor data, private user/project data, and user-supplied code data.
Principle (evidence first): accept public data only when source, provenance, license or redistribution status, contributor certification, and review disposition are recorded.

Principle (stop on protected-content risk): suspected standards text, tables, figures, examples, code-derived formulas, protected dimensional tables, proprietary catalogs, or private project/rule-pack data are blockers, not cleanup tasks.
Principle (human authority remains external): maintainers can review repository governance acceptance, but the workflow does not create legal clearance or professional engineering approval.

Principle (TBD is safer than invention): unresolved contributor legal mechanism, legal sufficiency, maintainer, release, or redistribution questions stay visible until decided by the appropriate human authority.

UnitStatement: Principle (local evidence first): the current-basis refresh reads the existing draft CONTRIBUTING.md section and certification template as evidence without editing repo-level policy files.
The workflow should be strict enough to prevent accidental public redistribution of protected or private data, but simple enough for contributors to complete before maintainer review.
A missing source or license should not be converted into a reviewer guess, and a permissive-looking public web page is not automatically a redistribution grant.
Reviewer notes should distinguish factual evidence from assumptions and proposals.
When a contribution includes engineering values, reviewer disposition should focus on public-repository acceptability and provenance, not engineering adequacy for project reliance.
Trade-off (contributor friction): more fields slow contribution intake; preferred posture is to keep fields minimal but mandatory for public data records.
Trade-off (source-rights uncertainty): fast acceptance is tempting when data looks useful; preferred posture is to preserve TBD or reject/quarantine until rights are documented.
Trade-off (protected-content detection): automated checks may miss paraphrased or reformatted protected data; preferred posture is to use automated gates as evidence aids plus human review.
Trade-off (maintainer authority): maintainers need a clear merge gate; preferred posture is to treat maintainer disposition as repository governance only.

The draft certification text has the contributor certify for repository-governance review that the contribution is original or submitted with documented redistribution rights, all sources/licenses/provenance are identified, and no protected standards text/tables/figures/examples/proprietary/private/rule-pack content is copied except where redistribution rights are documented.

Procedure step 1: assign an intake record ID using the future project convention, or TBD if no convention exists.
Procedure step 2: collect required provenance fields source_name, source_location, source_license, contributor, contributor_certification, redistribution_status, and review_status.
Procedure step 3: if source, license, contributor certification, or redistribution status is missing, set review status to pending or rejected with a TBD note.
Procedure step 3: do not infer redistribution rights from usefulness or public availability.

Procedure step 4: screen for protected standards text, tables, figures, examples, copied formulas, material allowables, SIF/flexibility tables, protected dimensional tables, proprietary vendor catalog data, commercial software examples/templates, private project data, private rule packs, owner standards, or company design bases.
Procedure step 4: if protected/private content is suspected, stop intake and set redistribution_status=protected_suspected or an equivalent note.
Procedure step 5: when quarantining suspected submissions, do not reproduce the suspected content in public notes.
Procedure step 5: move or reference the artifact only through quarantine/protected-content/ or a maintainer-approved equivalent.
Procedure step 5: treat quarantine access rule, escalation owner, and final legal disposition as TBD until human/legal authority records them.
Procedure step 5: record issue metadata, not protected content, and request human/legal review.
Procedure step 6: provenance-complete and public-permissive contributions proceed to maintainer review.
Procedure step 6: unknown, private-only, or protected-suspected contributions do not enter public examples or libraries.
Procedure step 6: legal or license uncertainty remains TBD pending human/legal decision.
Procedure step 7: record disposition using one of pending, accepted, rejected, or quarantined.
Procedure step 7: include reviewer, date, evidence reviewed, rationale, and limitations in the disposition.
Procedure step 7: state that disposition is repository governance review only and not engineering approval.
Procedure step 8: treat CONTRIBUTING.md and governance/CONTRIBUTOR_CERTIFICATION_TEMPLATE.md as draft governance surfaces until human acceptance.
Procedure step 8: edit repo-level contributor artifacts only under an explicitly approved write scope.

Procedure step 8: carry the selected project license as PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0; keep exact contributor legal mechanism, legal sufficiency, and reviewer/release authority TBD until recorded by the human project authority.

The deliverable defines local requirements and an evidence kit for a contributor certification workflow covering attestations, provenance fields, review routing, rejection rules, and quarantine handling for public data contributions.

The current-basis refresh does not edit repo-level artifacts, select the final contributor legal mechanism, assign final maintainer or reviewer authority, make legal conclusions, certify rights, or approve engineering reliance.

DEL-01-03-REQ-01: the workflow shall require contributor-provided source, location, license or TBD, contributor identity, certification statement, redistribution status, and review status for public data records.

DEL-01-03-REQ-02: the workflow shall reject or quarantine contributions with suspected protected standards text, tables, figures, examples, copied formulas, material allowables, SIF/flexibility tables, protected dimensional tables, proprietary vendor data without redistribution rights, or private user/project/rule-pack data.
DEL-01-03-REQ-03: the workflow shall route suspected protected content to human/legal review and shall not paraphrase protected tables or values into public data.

DEL-01-03-REQ-04: the workflow shall preserve TBD for unresolved contributor legal mechanism, maintainer authority, reviewer role, release authority, quorum, legal-review outcomes, and legal sufficiency of contribution instruments.

DEL-01-03-REQ-05: the workflow shall separate contribution governance from professional engineering approval and shall not claim certification, sealing, code compliance, legal clearance, or professional reliance.
DEL-01-03-REQ-06: the workflow shall record reviewer disposition as a project governance review only, with status values distinguishing pending, accepted, rejected, and quarantined contributions.
DEL-01-03-REQ-07: the workflow shall keep public/private data boundaries visible for future adapters, imports, rule packs, reports, and release gates.

DEL-01-03-REQ-08: the workflow shall maintain draft repo-level contributor workflow artifacts while keeping final contributor legal mechanism, legal sufficiency, reviewer authority, and human acceptance as separate governance decisions.
